summary: Frontend-only validation of PDF-blocked bug fix. Tested PDF rendering for peraturan + putusan via Katalog Peraturan and Tax Database list, for both uploaded-original files and text-generated PDFs, plus the two Unduh PDF download buttons. All 4 PDF rendering scenarios + 2 download scenarios pass. iframe src is a blob: URL in every case, no error fallback appears, and all /api/peraturan/{id}/pdf, /api/putusan/{id}/pdf and /api/files/{id}/download requests return 200 with no net::ERR_ABORTED. Bug 'mengapa saat menampilkan pdf diblokir' is FIXED.
critical_code_review_comments: PdfFrame fetches the PDF via axios responseType:'blob' and converts to blob: URL — this correctly sidesteps the preview proxy aborting direct iframe requests. Good fix.
Consider revoking the blob URL (URL.revokeObjectURL) in the PdfFrame cleanup effect to avoid memory leaks when users open many documents in a session.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (6/6 scenarios: peraturan uploaded, peraturan text-gen uu-7-2021, putusan uploaded, putusan text-gen put-pph21-2023, putusan Unduh PDF download, peraturan Unduh PDF download)

context_for_next_testing_agent: PDF viewer uses blob: URLs via PdfFrame (App.js ~line 13). Correct testids: per-doc-tab-pdf (peraturan tab), doc-tab-pdf (putusan tab), per-pdf-frame/per-pdf-frame-error, pdf-frame/pdf-frame-error, download-pdf-button, peraturan-download-pdf, database-open-peraturan-catalog, peraturan-item-{id}, database-putusan-{id}, database-peraturan-{id}. All endpoints verified: GET /api/peraturan/{id}/pdf?inline=1 -> 200, GET /api/putusan/{id}/pdf?inline=1 -> 200, GET /api/files/{id}/download?inline=1 -> 200. Headless Chromium renders the PDF plugin area as a grey rectangle on success — that is expected, not a failure.
rca of the issue: Original bug: PdfFrame earlier set <iframe src={backendUrl}> directly, and the preview proxy aborted the embedded cross-origin PDF request (net::ERR_ABORTED), so the iframe appeared blocked. Fix (now live): fetch the PDF via axios with responseType:'blob', wrap in URL.createObjectURL and use the resulting blob: URL as the iframe src. Verified: every PDF tab now produces src starting with 'blob:https://...', network requests complete 200, and the *-frame-error fallback never appears.
